lastText: File ClosedThe Ring, Closed After the FactMinor VictorySoviet High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: DECEMBER 1944 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around December 1944: earlier than the historical May 1945, bought with a faster, costlier advance. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over: a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The drive on Rostov closed the door on Army Group A: the encirclement history reached for and missed, landed on this path at the favorable edge of what the winter logistics allowed. The tank armies waited for the three fronts to close together and entered Prague on May 11, two days later than they did in the real war. The Seelow Heights fell on the second day instead of the third, at a lower cost: the best the plan could have done, and not what happened. No branch of this campaign reaches a different destination, only the timing and the price were ever in Soviet hands.One Year LaterVictory arrived ahead of the historical May 1945, which means the occupation of eastern and central Europe has had that much longer to harden by the time this account picks back up a year later.
